name: Fix the two defects in the new docs test suite: `qa/README.md` still declares the gate red, and the repo has no `package-lock.json`
description:
Two concrete, small defects in the test infrastructure delivered under card `09e338b9` (vitest + `qa/tests/site-integrity.test.mts`). Both are in the working tree, uncommitted. Neither is a redesign — do not change the assertions.

## Defect 1 — `qa/README.md` documents a red suite that is no longer red

`qa/README.md` lines 37-54 state:

```
## Current state — the gate is NOT green
**T3 fails today on `features/channel-creator.md`** ...
✗ T3 no orphan feature pages               (red on features/channel-creator.md)
 Tests  1 failed | 6 passed
```

That is no longer true. Card `07ba6b72` landed the link in the same working tree, so T3 passes:

- `.vitepress/config.mts:58` — `{ text: 'Channel content creator', link: '/features/channel-creator' }`
- `features/index.md:36` — `| [Channel content creator](/features/channel-creator) | ... |`

T3 (`reachableFeaturePages()`, `qa/tests/site-integrity.test.mts:117-123`) unions sidebar links with the body links of `features/index.md`, so the page is now reachable and the orphan set is empty.

Risk if not fixed: the sprint review on 2026-11-21 shows a documented failing gate that does not exist, and the cheapest way to "make the README true" is to add a `srcExclude` entry — which would remove a publishable feature page from the site. Correct the section to the real state and delete the "expected once the gate is healthy" block, or replace it with the actual command output.

**Acceptance:** run `npm test`, paste the verbatim output, and make the README match it line for line. If the real output is not 7 passing tests, say so and report which test disagrees — do not adjust the test to fit the README.

## Defect 2 — there is no `package-lock.json`, so `npm ci` is impossible

`project_locate("**/package-lock.json")` returns 0 matches: the repo has **no lockfile**. `qa/README.md:13-20` hedges around it ("`npm install` (not `npm ci`) for the first run ... after that run the lockfile is updated"), but nothing generates or commits it, so the suite is not reproducible: a fresh runner resolves whatever vitest 2.x is published that day.

**Do this:** run `npm install` once, which writes `package-lock.json`, commit that lockfile together with the `package.json` change (`vitest` added to `devDependencies`), then verify `npm ci && npm test` works from a clean `node_modules`. Update `qa/README.md` to the single strict form (`npm ci && npm test`) once the lockfile exists.

## Constraints

- Only these files: `package-lock.json` (new), `qa/README.md`. Do not touch `qa/tests/site-integrity.test.mts`, `.vitepress/config.mts` or `features/index.md`.
- Nothing here may be committed into the pending approval baseline (`a8be6182`) without the approval; if the tree is gated, produce the changes and say what is waiting.
- Report `git diff --stat` and the verbatim `npm test` output on the card.

## Why these profiles

`software_developer` — owns the runner, the lockfile and running `npm test`. `web_master` — owns the docs tree and the wording of `qa/README.md`.

messages.content: Read `qa/README.md` and `qa/tests/site-integrity.test.mts`, then fix the two defects described: (1) the README still declares T3 red on `features/channel-creator.md`, which card `07ba6b72` has already linked (`.vitepress/config.mts:58`, `features/index.md:36`); (2) the repo has no `package-lock.json`, so `npm ci` cannot run. Run `npm install` to generate the lockfile, run `npm test`, paste the verbatim output, and make the README match the real output exactly. Do not change the assertions and do not add a `srcExclude` entry to quiet anything.
